main_text.p: Dialectici referūt in numerum aduersorum, valetudinem & morbum: diem & noctem? At qui inter Philosophos constat, morbum nihil aliud esse, quàm priuationem valetudinis, & noctem diei, nam corpus terrę soli oppositum umbram efficit. Cicero ipse in Topicis Sapientiā & stultitiam, bonitatem & malitiam inter aduersorum exempla posuit. At Boëtius homo acutissimus, & in hoc disciplinæ genere omnium iudicio singularis, rectè admonuit, stultitiam esse priuationem sapientiæ: malitiā bonitatis. sic multi inter aduersorum exempla referunt calorem & frigus: humorem & siccitatem: cùm tamen à Physicis, disputetur frigus priuationem esse caloris, & siccitatem humoris.
main_text.head: De Medio in contrariis.
CAP. XXI.
main_text.p: VAE est altera Contrariorum summa diuisio? Vulgaris diuisio est huiusmodi, ut quædam tertium, siue medium, recipiant, quædā non recipiāt. nā in Aduersis, Relatis & Priuatibus, sunt quæ recipiāt: sunt & quæ nō recipiāt. In aientibus autem & negantibus, nulla mediū recipiunt.
Cedo exemplum de aduersis. In Aduersis hæc medium recipiunt: Candidum & atrum recipiunt fuscum, purpureum, viride, & alia nonnulla. Pulcher & deformis statam formā.

page.notes: The first word of the chapter is set with a large initial, read here as "VAE". The printed "V AE" may be a spacing artefact. The marks "?" after "diuisio" and "noctem" are printed question marks, not doubt marks. The long s is rendered as s throughout, and "funt" is read as "sunt". Reading "siccitatem" is based on the printed "ficcitatem", where the initial letter is a long s. No catchword or signature is visible at the foot.
